catalogueRuleDetailChangeAssessment.method: Every changed rule has identical fields except locations; locations compare as an identical multiset, preserving duplicate counts. These are presentation-order differences, not changes in status, requirement or observed locations.

limits: The compared3.6 preflight uses a development binary. The final release build/corpus result is a separate artifact owned by the release process.
Historical pass/fail filenames and clause/test numbers are provisional candidate mappings, not normative oracles. An unrelated failure never proves that a named atomic requirement was validated.
No conforming verdict was emitted. The1509 nonconforming and655 indeterminate outcomes do not constitute a complete ISO validation certificate or an accuracy score.
There are no corpus files selected as3a or3u in these snapshots. Synthetic cross-profile tests are separate evidence; this corpus comparison does not assert corpus coverage of all11 profiles.
Unchanged failed-rule/model-failure lists do not prove all failure detection is correct. The previously documented targeted case reviews and normative gaps remain relevant.
Nonfailure model status counts change when new native models are added. Those counts alone do not prove normative coverage or a reduction of all unknowns.

No production Swift source or corpus PDF was modified during this independent review; the research script uses original standard-library comparisons and hashing, with no external PDF validation engine.

finalRelease.comparison: All per-file Release results equal frozen preflight after sorting unordered diagnostic location arrays;24files differ only by location order. Historical filenames are provisional, not an accuracy/completeness oracle.
